They were briefly different -- directory `folio-assistant-core`, name `folio-assist-core` -- and this comment went on asserting the short name after the `name` field beside it had already been changed, so the file contradicted itself in adjacent lines. Corrected 2026-09-20. WHAT IS STILL SHORT, DELIBERATELY, IS THE LANDING CARD ID below: a card id is a PUBLISHED IDENTIFIER and does not move with a directory. `landing-sticky.test.ts` says so and bean `8xtj` records the cost of assuming the two are one string -- a session sweeping every spelling at once renamed the card by accident and had to put it back. Main created a folio-assistant-core/ stub the same day; the two were one instance under two paths, and instanceRoots is keyed on the declared name, so the stub and the populated one collided on one key and the stub won. Consolidated here, declared as a real instance on the owner's ruling of 2026-09-20 ("Create f-a-core/ as a real instance now"). It declared NO directories when it was created, deliberately, because the modules it would own were still interleaved under cat-harness/ and declaring a directory that is not there is the dh4f defect. They are NOT interleaved any more: bean frs5's branch wrote `schemas/` (dublin-core, catalogue, materialization, library-ref) and `folios/`, and they moved in here rather than staying under a SECOND directory declaring this same name. Two instances with one declared name is not a layout question: `instanceRoots` is keyed on the declared name, so the stub and the populated one were one key and the stub won. The original note read: the modules it will own are still interleaved with the harness's under cat-harness/, and declaring a directory that is not there is the dh4f defect — every consumer then scans nothing and reports a clean run over it. An instance that declares only what it has is honest; one that declares its target layout is a lie a gate cannot catch. scripts/repo-partition.ts is the machine-readable statement of what will move here.

stickies.body:
The knowledge graph is four sub-graphs, and an instance declares which of them it holds.

**Content** is what somebody authors and a reader reads — this layer's subject. **Skills** are the instructions an agent follows to do the work. **Processes** are the BPMN diagrams that say who does what, in which order, and where the gates are — they are executable, not illustrations. **Tools** are what an agent can call.

Getting anything in is **acquisition**: unstructured and semi-structured sources arrive through `uploads/` or through the conversation, and are ingested into `library/`. It is a step rather than a graph kind of its own — there is no fifth directory to look for.

**Scope:** the content model — what a folio IS. Not the skills and tools that operate on it, and not any particular folio's chapters.

directories.description: The schemas of the content layer's Node Kinds, kept as their own Subgraph until this repository is split.
directories._description_comment: The content layer's own schema nodes. Three today, and they are one chain: `dublin-core` is what a source system SAYS about an item, `catalogue` is the shape of the collection that item sits in, and `materialization` is whether any of its bytes are actually here. The third is the load-bearing one — see its module doc for why bootstrap fetching a harness and who-iris fetching three items out of 361.55 GB are the same process with two names.

directories.description: What an AUTHOR creates using the graph -- a note, a visualization, a paper. Owner, 2026-09-20: 'folios/ would be a note, visualization, paper etc that user/author is creating referencing the KG... folios in f-a-core as it is about KG management workflows built on cat-harness document rendering justthedocs simple rendering.' It declares the EXISTING `folio` kind rather than a new one: `folio` is already 'authored content, rendered to a website', registered by core because only core can render it, and a second kind for the same thing would be two spellings of one concept. The contrast is with `docs` in cat-harness, whose subject is the harness itself. Worked example of the distinction: the who-iris catalogue goes in `library/` or is referenced remotely; a note ABOUT it is a folio; the page explaining how ingestion works is docs.

Core's glossary (owner, 2026-09-23: "put glossary into folio-assistant-core", "part of general pracice w/ glossary/ page"): folio-glossary/v1 documents, each a SKOS concept scheme of local terms linked to external SKOS concepts by exactMatch/closeMatch, plus external concepts listed as members without being copied. A whole external scheme is referenced through remoteGraphs with graphKinds ["glossary"]. `dependents: reproduce` so every folio built on core gets its own glossary/, which is what makes a glossary general practice rather than a harness feature. Rendered on the glossary/ page with the swimlane ledger (cat-harness's `swimlane-glossary`) as one more source; checked by `check:glossary`.

The content layer's Tool nodes. Declared 2026-09-22 with the first one, `folio-changeset` (bean jwox, epic q4jm), which exposes `schemas/changeset.ts`. Reached by the harness through tool auto-discovery (bean p0za, owner ruling 2026-09-22), never by an import: the harness may not import core, and a Tool node is a declaration loaded by path.

The content layer's own ContentAdapters. `document/` arrived 2026-09-30 as step 2 of the adapters closure (bean `ybp4`, planned in `r0tm`, ruled by the owner as option A: two PRs, paper first). It took the `cat-harness ->` sibling-import count from 2 to 0 — the last two escapes were `intake-records.ts` and its test, both importing `schemas/dublin-core.js` UP out of the harness, and both are now intra-instance. The remedy is `yj6r`'s throughout: the CONSUMER moves up and the schema stays; no schema moved down into `cat-harness/schemas/`, which that bean forbids as buying a green gate by relocating the boundary the gate protects. The directory's own imports into `cat-harness/src/`, `cat-harness/schemas/` and `cat-harness/content/pipeline/` are DOWNWARD and therefore legal — core declares `needs: ["cat-harness"]`. Its six consuming tests moved with it into `scripts/tests/`, because a test does not leave its subject to make a count fall. Three things shipped in the same commit because each fails SILENTLY rather than loudly: this declaration, `tsconfig.json`'s `include` entry (without it `bun run typecheck` goes green while covering twelve fewer files, and no gate reports a shrinking program), and the `BUILTIN_ADAPTERS` module path — which is resolved by VARIABLE specifier, so no static-import gate would have caught it. `paper/` is not here: it is the science layer's and lives in `folio-assistant-sci/adapters/paper/` since bean `y5si`, step 1 of the same closure.

Core's own server half: the HTTP routes that act on a folio's CONTENT — `routes/feedback.ts` (its feedback items), `routes/glossary.ts` (its glossary candidates), `routes/relevance.ts` (its bibliography relevance). Moved up from `cat-harness/src/routes/` when the server moved to `cat-harness-tools` (bean `70lx`, B1; owner, 2026-10-04: a content package's server half lives with its content). The server declares them by their `src/routes/*` path and finds them here through `needs`, since core needs `cat-harness-tools`; they import the server's contract (`route-groups`, `types`, `core/rbac`) DOWN from it.

Core's own executable surface, with every test beside its subject: the review-comment Tool and its move helper, the glossary extractors, the sample-import pair, and — since bean `yj6r`, 2026-09-30 — two tranches of escapes that moved UP out of `cat-harness/`. The materialisation trio (`check-materialized-fixity`, `backfill-materialized-fixity`, `cache-index`) and the FHIR IG artefact-index pair (`ingest-ig-artifacts`, `check-artifact-index`) came first, to sit beside the `schemas/materialization.ts` and `schemas/fhir-artifact-index.ts` they read. The glossary CLUSTER followed — `build-glossary.ts`, its `:refterm` codemod `codemod-refterm.ts`, and all three of their tests — because walking a paper's blocks to collect `defines[]` and emit a `folio-glossary/v1` scheme is CONTENT machinery, and the harness (`needs: ["bootstrap"]`) was importing upward into this instance's `schemas/glossary.ts` and `scripts/glossary-page.ts` — an import against its own declaration, and a circular dependency between repositories after the split. The partition rules already classified `content/pipeline/` as core, so the classification did not change; the DIRECTORY caught up with it. They are still addressed as pipeline scripts by id, and `resolvePipelineScript` searches the folio, then the platform, then here. The LAST FOUR clusters followed on the same day and in the same tranche, taking the `cat-harness ->` sibling-import count from 5 to 2: `extract-assets.ts` (a container a folio was given → a `folio-extraction/v1` record, reading `schemas/extraction.ts` — both moved DOWN again on 2026-10-02 by owner ruling 2 of the placement proposal, bean `tlat`: the script to `cat-harness-tools/scripts/`, the schema to `cat-harness/schemas/`, as the tool behind the harness's own `asset-extraction` skill), `check-voices.ts` (every voice rule's citation resolved through `schemas/library-ref.ts` into a folio's `library/`), and `build-document-site.ts` WITH its test, which reads `schemas/changeset.ts`. The last is the one with an invocation surface: a DOCUMENT folio's generated staging workflow names it by path, so `init-folio.ts` now writes `folio-assistant-core/scripts/build-document-site.ts` and `init-folio.test.ts` pins that string — the same instance-relative property this entry records for `review-comments.ts`, arrived at from the other direction. The partition rules had already classified all four `core` by exact entry, so again only the DIRECTORY moved; each dead entry was removed with its reasoning kept in place, because a rule naming a path its own scan can no longer see fires on nothing while reading as an adjudication. The adapters closure followed on the same day: `adapters/document/` and its SIX consuming tests are now here and in `adapters/`, taking the count 2 -> 0 (bean `ybp4`). This sentence previously read "What did NOT move, and deliberately" of those two files, and recorded that the closure "needs its own ruling" — it got one, and `r0tm`'s re-derivation also corrected the deterrent measurement: the 15 created escapes were 16, and paper-first is FREE, which is what turned an all-or-nothing three-instance move into two ordinary steps. This sentence listed only the review-comment pair until then, by which point four other tools were already here — a directory description that names its founding file rather than its contents goes stale the first time anything lands. Core declared its `schemas/`, its `folios/`, its `voices/` and its `tools/` and left `scripts/` undeclared, which is the `ylj7` shape: the directories that hold what is DESCRIBED were declared and the one holding what RUNS was not. Declared where it is: `review-comments.ts` is invoked by path from `folio-staging.yml`, so relocating it is an invocation surface `check:workflow-paths` would have to re-guard for nothing the declaration does not already buy.

L1 source content this LAYER owns — the publications core's own vocabulary is derived FROM, one `<bib-slug>/` per ingested document. Declared 2026-09-23 on the owner's ruling that Doc-Researcher (arXiv:2510.21603v1) is part of the f-a-c subgraph, and declared rather than borrowed for the reason `methodology-adoption` §4 gives: a method is placed by OWNERSHIP so that extraction is literal, and a paper core's methodology cites from another instance's library would not lift out with it. `ingest-document.ts` refuses to guess a destination when several are declared, which is what surfaced the absence. `dependents: skip` because these are THIS layer's sources; a downstream folio's library is its own and reproducing these would hand it somebody else's corpus.

The methodologies core adopts from its own corpus. Separate from `cat-harness/methodologies/` for the reason `smart-base-methodologies` is separate from both: a method belongs to the layer whose job it describes, so the directory lifts out with this instance and nothing else moves. Core's job, per this instance's AGENTS.md, is what a folio HOLDS, where it CAME FROM and how much is PRESENT — which is why a document-ingestion method is core's and not the harness's.

The skills core owns. `skills/voices/` is declared separately above as the `voices` kind: a voice partitions how prose READS and is a different graph from an instruction body, so the nesting is two kinds in one place rather than one kind declared twice.

The BPMN core owns -- `deep-document-research`, Doc-Researcher's iterative loop as an executable process. A TOP-LEVEL directory rather than `methodologies/processes/`, which is where it was first put: `check:layout-norms` refused that as a package subdirectory of an already-declared graph, declaring the same directory twice. `smart-base` carries the nested shape and is baselined, but the harness's own diagrams live in a top-level `processes/` and so do these. That satisfies bean `g43o` -- `workflowDirs` resolves from a DECLARED directory -- without the double declaration, which is strictly better than baselining a third instance of a tolerated exception.

What auditing THIS instance produced, committed so a consumer can tell "never audited" from "audited clean" — a printed verdict cannot, which is why every QA verdict here is a sidecar. TWO kinds live here and the files declare which they are via $schema: kg-qa/v1, one per audited subject, in a tree mirroring the subject’s own path, and ONE kg-qa-manifest/v1 recording the auditor’s identity for all of them. The manifest moved here from skills/ on 2026-09-27: kg-audit.ts writes it unconditionally, so its old home created a skills/ directory holding no skills in every instance that has none. At declaration time that is 7 files across processes (1), scenarios (1), skills (1), tools (4). No qa-results/v1 and no witnesses: this instance runs no document build and no witness-producing computation, and declaring kinds it does not hold would be an over-claim. dependents: reproduce, because a dependent audits its OWN graph — these verdicts are about this instance’s nodes, and inheriting them would attribute one instance’s findings to another. Declared WITH its files in one commit, per bean dh4f: a declared-but-absent directory makes a consumer scan nothing and report a clean run over it.

_needs_comment: The layer this instance sits on. Owner, 2026-09-20: "So bootsteap, cat harness, fa-core, f-a, from bottom to top." Declared rather than hardcoded in the navbar, so the ordering is a fact of the repository and not of whichever consumer needed it first. `cat-harness-tools` added 2026-10-01 on owner ruling C1 (epic 7x5n, bean rmi6): the tool implementation layer sits BELOW this one, so core may use it and it may never use core.
_contentAdapters_comment: Declared HERE, by the instance that ships the adapter, so cat-harness's composition root (`src/builtin-adapters.ts`) finds it by reading declarations instead of holding a `../folio-assistant-core/adapters/document/index.ts` path into the layer above it. That path was the last upward import out of cat-harness, and a variable one no static gate could see (bean p11x, `check:import-direction`).
